subject: Geo-fidelity DPA: subprocessor roster and transient failover protocol
messages:
From: Alex Russo <alex.russo@healthsync.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Geo-fidelity and temporary cross-region hops — DPA clarifications

Elliot / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this early look. We're doing a security + procurement evaluation ahead of our pilot and have two items we need explicit language on before we sign:

1) "Geo-fidelity" commitment: We need confirmation that customer production data for HealthSync will remain physically processed in the region we designate (US-East) except for well-defined transient failover scenarios. Please confirm the default SLA (region-only processing) and the scope of acceptable transient cross-region hops (duration, purpose, and telemetry).

2) Subprocessor roster + evidence: Please provide current roster and a timeline for SOC2 / audit evidence for new subprocessors added in the next 90 days. Our legal team prefers to see the roster in CSV.

I've attached our latest DPA (HealthSync_DPA_v3.pdf) with comments in the margin. Two asks: can you (a) confirm the transient failover max window (we typically request <= 72 hours) and (b) provide a proposed short DPA addendum clause that covers transient replication for failover/cache warming?

Appreciate a concise reply — we have procurement deadlines next Friday.

— Alex
Alex Russo
Head of Security, HealthSync
Attachment: HealthSync_DPA_v3.pdf (pdf, 84KB)

From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-fidelity and temporary cross-region hops — DPA clarifications

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step and links to artifacts.

1) Geo-fidelity commitment: Redwood supports per-customer region affinity for production workloads. For customers who elect "geo-fidelity" (region pin = US-East in your case) we guarantee that primary inference requests and persisted telemetry are processed and stored in the pinned region. We do allow transient, operational-only hops for high-availability or cache-warming; our standard operational window is up to 72 hours for short-lived KV/cache replication during failover or planned maintenance. All transient copies are: encrypted at rest and in transit, access-logged, and scope-limited to serving runtime caches (not long-term storage).

2) Subprocessor roster + evidence: Attached is our current roster (redwood_subprocessors_q2.csv). New subprocessors are added to the roster with 30 days' notice; for high-risk additions we provide SOC2 evidence or equivalent. We can commit to providing SOC2 attestations for any subprocessors that will handle decrypted data paths.

Proposed DPA addendum language (high level): "Redwood may perform temporary, automated cross-region replication for ephemeral cache or failover purposes for up to 72 hours; such replication is limited to in-memory/KV artifacts, encrypted, and logged; Redwood will notify customer and provide telemetry for any event exceeding standard operational windows." I can put a draft addendum in DocuSign if that helps.

Artifacts included: redwood_geo_fidelity_response.pdf (explanation + diagram), redwood_subprocessors_q2.csv (roster). Also I pasted a short canary plan below for confirmation.

Canary plan (ops):
- Pilot for HealthSync only: 24h canary where we exercise a controlled failover to the secondary region using synthetic requests.
- Telemetry: tokenized request IDs + region hop logs provided to HealthSync support only.
- Rollback: automatic rollback to pinned region once primary capacity restores; transient copies purged per policy.

If you want, Marissa can jump into legal wording. If these are acceptable, I'll push a DPA addendum draft and we can route through your legal/procurement.

— Elliot
Elliot Price
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_geo_fidelity_response.pdf (pdf, 96KB); redwood_subprocessors_q2.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Alex Russo <alex.russo@healthsync.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthsync.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: 2027-06-24T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-fidelity and temporary cross-region hops — DPA clarifications

Elliot — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement:

• Can you confirm the exact telemetry fields you'll provide for any transient hop event (we need timestamp, source region, target region, request IDs, and duration)?
• We need a firm maximum: 72 hours is acceptable only if there is an automated purge at the end of the window and an alert if any replica persists beyond that time.

Legal has asked for a DocuSign route for the addendum. Can you generate a short DPA addendum (1–2 paragraphs) that includes the purge and notification commitments and a clause that new subprocessors that may access decrypted data require advance notice + SOC2 evidence within 30 days? If you can send the DocuSign link and a short summary line for procurement that would speed things.

Also copying procurement — we will block the pilot approval until the addendum is signed, but the pilot can proceed under a narrow exception if Redwood agrees to the telemetry and purge confirmations.

— Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthsync.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: 2027-06-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-fidelity and temporary cross-region hops — DPA clarifications

Alex — appreciate the patience while we drafted formal language.

I've attached a one-paragraph DPA addendum draft (DPA_addendum_draft.docx) that reflects the 72-hour transient window, mandatory automated purge at T+72, required telemetry fields (timestamp, source_region, target_region, request_id, duration), and the notification trigger (email + signed audit artifact) if any replica persists beyond the window. It also includes the subprocessor clause: advance notice for new subprocessors and SOC2-or-equivalent attestation within 30 days for any subprocessor with access to decrypted runtime paths.

Next steps I propose:
- Elliot to upload the addendum to DocuSign by EOD tomorrow.
- HealthSync to review and send back any redlines within 48 hours to avoid blocking the pilot.
- If you need a limited exception to start the pilot before signature, we can provision a time-limited, tightly scoped exception with enhanced monitoring and a dedicated support contact.

If that works I'll route the DocuSign and include the HubSpot summary line for procurement.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA_addendum_draft.docx (docx, 6KB)
